chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Musiwi narrated to me from Ubaydillah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He said to a man: O so-and-so! What prevents you, when a need arises for you, from going to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), praying four Rak'ahs there, and then asking for your need? Verily, the obligatory prayer performed there equals a Hajj, and the Nafilah prayer equals an 'Umrah.

key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for praying at the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) highlights the spiritual potency of the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as a locus for divine acceptance, linking physical proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt with immense eschatological rewards. The equivalence of the obligatory prayer to Hajj and the voluntary prayer to Umrah underscores the concept of *fadilah* (virtue) inherent in the Imams' resting places, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the merit of specific locations for worship.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm Al-Mūsawi narrated to me from ‘Ubaydillāh ibn Nahīk, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from someone who said: Abu Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.))

said to a man: O so-and-so! What prevents you at times of need from going to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), praying four Rak’ah, and then asking (Allāh) for your needs?! Verily establishing an obligatory prayer next to his grave is equal to performing a Hajj and establishing a Nāfilah prayer (next to his grave) is equal to performing an ‘Umrah.
